paths.title: Expert path: recognise by the first check, page to the bedside, prepare, inotrope in phase 2
Early escalation, but phase 2 treats low output with more fluid then a pressor
Recognised after the second check; surgeon paged just inside 20 minutes: re-exploration by a slower route
Recognised at the second check, called at 20 minutes without preparing: bedside resternotomy
Routine call gets phone orders; the second call brings the surgeon late; bedside resternotomy
Fluids and a pressor without escalation: PEA arrest
Expert live phase, then ends phase 2 without a decision
Arrest, then the cardiac-surgery protocol: compressions at once, resternotomy called, no full-dose epinephrine
paths.notes: Tap-to-the-beat compressions at 110 a minute with 6 s pauses; ROSC when the chest is open (10 min without the tray). Recovered: ROSC after an arrest is rescue (9.2).

paths.title: Arrest: compressions and resternotomy, but 1 mg epinephrine without expert direction
paths.notes: STS 2017 names epinephrine during an arrest after cardiac surgery as harmful (class III) unless an experienced clinician directs it; the harm shows at ROSC.

paths.title: Arrest with paced compressions (no tapping): a shock to PEA, fluid first, resternotomy late
paths.notes: The accessible compression mode, scored on the rate and pause chosen. A shock to a non-shockable rhythm, a wrong fix first, the right one after 3 minutes.

paths.title: The expert path at study pace (3x)
paths.notes: REQ-209. The expert path with pace 3 logged first, a teaching answer for each prompt (one deliberately wrong) and a chapter 'continue' at each break. Pacing, teaching and chapter commands change no sim state, so the end state, criteria, KPIs and state hash are the expert path's own; only the fewest wall seconds differ.

paths.title: A focused start at study pace (3x)
paths.notes: REQ-209. begin focused (evolves the normal start to tick 780 with no actions), pace 3, then an expert-style path from there. The tubes criterion is not applicable because the start is after the expert's recognition time (540 s); every other criterion is scored as in a full case.
